lessonActivities.title: Time & Place Expression Changes 🕐📍
lessonActivities.content:
Here's where it gets interesting! 🌍 Many learners forget that time and place words also change in reported speech. Let's clarify:

FeatureDirect SpeechReported Speech
Time: Now'I'm busy now.'She said she was busy then.
Time: Today'I'll call today.'He said he would call that day.
Time: Yesterday'I saw her yesterday.'She said she had seen her the day before.
Time: Tomorrow'We leave tomorrow.'They said they left the next day.
Place: Here'Sit here.'She told me to sit there.
Place: This'I like this book.'He said he liked that book.

The secret: Imagine you're reporting the conversation from a different time or place. Words like 'here' and 'today' no longer make sense! 🗺️

Common mistake: 'He said he is coming tomorrow' × → Correct: 'He said he was coming the next day' ✓

Fun fact: If you report speech on the same day, 'today' can sometimes stay 'today'! Context matters! 📅

Pro tip: Look for time/place words in direct speech. If the reporting context has changed, shift them: today→that day, here→there.
examples: Time change: 'I finished yesterday' → She said she had finished the day before.
Place change: 'Meet me here' → He told me to meet him there.
Wrong vs Right: 'She said she is leaving tomorrow' × → 'She said she was leaving the next day' ✓
functions: Adjusting time expressions for reported context
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: Look for time/place words in direct speech. If the reporting context has changed, shift them: today→that day, here→there.

lessonActivities.title: Contextual Reporting: When Expressions Don't Change 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Advanced insight! 🎯 Sometimes time/place expressions don't change in reported speech. It depends on when and where you're reporting.

Rule: If the time/place reference is still accurate when you report, keep the original word.

ScenarioDirect SpeechReported (Same Day)Reported (Later)
Today (reported same day)'I'm busy today.'She said she's busy today.She said she was busy that day.
Here (same location)'Meet me here.'He told me to meet him here.He told me to meet him there.
Now (immediate reporting)'I'm leaving now.'She says she's leaving now.She said she was leaving then.

Fun fact: Native speakers often mix rules in casual speech—focus on clarity first! 💬

Master level: In formal writing, be consistent with shift rules. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!
examples: Same-day reporting: 'I'll call today' → He said he'll call today (if still today).
Different location: 'This is my office' → She said that was her office.
Immediate context: 'It's raining now' → She says it's raining now (if still raining).
functions: Determining when expressions change vs. stay
lessonActivities.tips: Master level: In formal writing, be consistent with shift rules. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!

writingActivities.question: Report what your friend said yesterday about their plans. Include: a time expression change and a place expression change.
writingActivities.hint: Change 'today'→'that day', 'here'→'there'. Example: She said she would meet me there that day.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct time expression change:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw her yesterday.' → Reported: He said he had seen her ______.
gameActivities.hint: 'Yesterday' in direct speech usually becomes 'the day before' in reported speech.

badges.message: You never mix up 'yesterday' and 'the day before' again!
